q2.answer: The position is `sync_state.download_cursor` in `catalogue.db`, which holds the id of the last product in the last fully saved page. It is updated in the same SQLite transaction that upserts that page into `products_staging`, so the saved rows and the cursor always match, and a page that was not committed is simply fetched again.

q3.answer: Before the first page, the client records a watermark from `GET /position`. Because `change_seq` is assigned at commit and rows become visible in order, every later edit, insert or delete has a `change_seq` above the watermark. After the last page, the client replays `GET /changes?since=watermark` into staging, and it also does a catch-up partway through if the watermark is more than 3 days old, so it stays inside the tombstone window.

q5.answer: It is built in a separate `products_staging` table in `catalogue.db` while the old `products` table stays live: pages first, then the catch-up, then the indexes. It becomes the catalogue the app reads when one SQLite transaction drops `products`, renames staging to `products` and sets `live_position` to the watermark; screens then reload.

q9.answer: It upserts the row only if the incoming `change_seq` is at least the one already stored, so replays and overlaps between pages and catch-up keep the newest version. A delete entry removes the row if it is present.

q10.answer: It starts from `sync_state.live_position`, which is set to the download's final watermark at the swap. It moves forward to `next_since` in the same transaction that applies each response of up to 1,000 changes, so the position never runs ahead of the applied data.

q11.answer: The server reads the Postgres products table, tombstones included, with `WHERE change_seq > :since ORDER BY change_seq LIMIT 1001` on a new `change_seq` index. Before that it checks `since` against `catalogue_sync_meta.purge_horizon` and returns 410 if `since` is older. A delete is sent as `{ id, change_seq, deleted: true }` from the soft-deleted row, and each product appears once, in its current state.
